title: Council Districts 2, 3 and 4 are on the November 3, 2026 ballot
body: Fremont holds its General Municipal Election on November 3, 2026. Voters in Districts 2, 3 and 4 choose their councilmembers. The City's election page lists the candidates and a tool to find your district.

title: Council defers a possible half-cent sales tax measure
body: News reports say the Council voted unanimously to defer a half-cent sales tax measure instead of placing it on the November 2026 ballot. City staff are expected to return with other ways to close the funding gap.

title: FY 2026/27 budget adopted with no room to restore earlier cuts
body: The Council adopted the FY 2026/27 Operating Budget on June 9, 2026. The proposed budget kept staffing and services at current-year levels, including the FY 2025/26 reductions, and said there was no capacity to restore eliminated positions or services.
source_title: FY 2026/27 Proposed Budget presentation, May 12, 2026 (City of Fremont)

title: City says 10 more Human Services positions will be eliminated
body: A March 30, 2026 letter from the City Manager says State and federal funding changes will require eliminating 10 more positions in the Human Services Department, which provides safety-net services. The City has not said which programs are affected.
source_title: City Manager letter to Sen. Wahab and Asm. Lee, March 30, 2026

title: Budget rebalancing approved: reductions in every department
body: On February 10, 2026 the Council approved reductions in staffing, overtime, training and contract services to cover $3.8 million in new labor costs. The Police Department eliminated six administrative positions, two detention officers and one detention supervisor. No sworn police or fire positions were cut.
source_title: City Council Approves Budget Rebalancing (City of Fremont, Feb 13, 2026)

title: About $3 million less for streets, parks and medians
body: To balance the FY 2025/26 budget adopted on June 10, 2025, the City reduced infrastructure maintenance spending by about $3 million. A later City letter describes this as pavement maintenance and park and street-median capital replacement.
source_title: City Council Approves Budget Rebalancing (City of Fremont, Feb 13, 2026)
